o1.biggest_strength: Tells me the brutal truth: the pause does 80% of the work and the flow is worse than today without it, then backs it with a working range (+1,230 to +1,680) instead of a single fantasy number.
o1.biggest_mistake: The 'Cancel my subscription' button is only active once a reason is picked — that is exactly the 'don't make me hunt' friction Lena hates. It should stay live, with the reason required only to finish, not to unlock cancel.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep cancel live from the first tap, and present the £29,160 discount saving as per-cohort or steady-state so a finance reader can't misread it.

o2.biggest_strength: More granular per-reason offers (a smaller daily goal for people who already have a reminder, a 'remind me later' for trip-over) and it keeps the cancel button live and never greyed out.
o2.biggest_mistake: The switching-apps line counts 67 half-price keepers at the full £9 (£607, labelled 'after discount'), and the £136k first-year figure multiplies by 12 with no churn — I can't take that to finance without recutting it.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the discounted value, apply the 6% monthly churn, add an honest range, and drop or test the unexplained 50% offer to switchers.

reason: Output 1 is the one I'd send to the product team: it tells me the pause is the whole game, gives numbers I can defend with a real range, and keeps the copy in our voice. Output 2 is tidy, but I caught a wrong revenue figure and no churn, so I'd have to rework the money before trusting it.
